title: Transfer Case Control System (MIL Request)
plain: The transfer case control module (the computer that runs four-wheel drive) found a fault and asked the engine computer to turn on the check engine light.
symptoms: Check engine light on
4WD may not engage or may be stuck in one mode
4WD indicator may flash

causes.name: Fault stored in the transfer case control module
Transfer case shift motor or position sensor problem
Wiring or connector fault at the transfer case

checks: Scan the transfer case module for its own codes, which point to the real problem
Check the transfer case shift motor connector for corrosion
fix: Fix the fault stored in the transfer case module; this code clears once that problem is repaired.

title: Reverse Inhibit Control Circuit
plain: There is an electrical problem in the circuit that blocks reverse gear when the car is moving forward. This is mostly found on some manual transmissions.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Reverse may be hard or impossible to select
Or reverse may not be blocked while moving

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector at the solenoid

checks: Inspect the solenoid connector on the side of the transmission
Test the solenoid resistance and its power supply
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the reverse lockout solenoid.

title: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit/Open
plain: The wire the transmission computer uses to ask the engine computer to turn on the check engine light has an open or electrical fault.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Broken wire between the transmission and engine computers
Loose or corroded connector at either module

checks: Check the transmission computer for its own stored codes
Check the request wire between the modules for an open
fix: Repair the open wire or connector between the transmission and engine computers.

title: 1-4 Upshift (Skip Shift) Solenoid Control Circuit
plain: On some manual transmissions, a solenoid forces a shift from 1st straight to 4th during light driving to save fuel. The computer found an electrical problem in that solenoid circuit.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Skip shift may stop working, or shifter may block 2nd gear unexpectedly

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector at the solenoid

checks: Inspect the solenoid connector on the transmission
Test the solenoid resistance and its power supply
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the skip shift solenoid.
examples: Known on manual-transmission Chevrolet Corvette and Camaro models with the 1-to-4 skip shift feature

title: 1-4 Upshift (Skip Shift) Lamp Control Circuit
plain: The dash light that tells you the car will shift from 1st straight to 4th has an electrical problem in its control circuit.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Skip shift light on the dash may not work or stay on

causes.name: Burned-out bulb or failed instrument cluster indicator

checks: Check whether the skip shift light works during the bulb check at start-up
Check the lamp circuit wiring for an open or short
fix: Repair the lamp circuit wiring or the indicator in the instrument cluster.
examples: Known on manual-transmission Chevrolet Corvette and Camaro models with the 1-to-4 skip shift feature

title: Clutch Position Sensor Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the clutch position sensor, which tells the computer how far the clutch pedal is pressed, or how far an automated clutch is engaged.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine may not crank, or cruise control may not work
Jerky clutch engagement on automated manual transmissions

causes.name: Broken or damaged wiring to the clutch position sensor
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the clutch position sensor for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the clutch position sensor against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the clutch position sensor.

title: Clutch Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The clutch position sensor is giving readings that don't match what the computer expects for the current conditions. The clutch position sensor tells the computer how far the clutch pedal is pressed, or how far an automated clutch is engaged.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine may not crank, or cruise control may not work
Jerky clutch engagement on automated manual transmissions

causes.name: Sensor out of adjustment or not calibrated
Clutch hydraulic problem or worn clutch
High resistance in the wiring or connector
Control module software needs an update

checks: Compare the clutch position sensor reading with what it should be on a scan tool
Inspect the wiring and connector for corrosion or damage
fix: Correct any fluid or wiring problem first; if the readings are still wrong, replace the clutch position sensor.

title: Clutch Position Sensor Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the clutch position sensor circuit that is lower than it should be. The clutch position sensor tells the computer how far the clutch pedal is pressed, or how far an automated clutch is engaged.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine may not crank, or cruise control may not work
Jerky clutch engagement on automated manual transmissions

causes.name: Wire shorted to ground in the clutch position sensor circuit

checks: Inspect the clutch position sensor wiring for chafed spots touching metal
Check the circuit for a short to ground with a meter
Unplug the clutch position sensor and see whether the reading changes
fix: Fix any shorted or damaged wiring; if the wiring is good, replace the clutch position sensor.

title: Clutch Position Sensor Circuit High
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the clutch position sensor circuit that is higher than it should be. The clutch position sensor tells the computer how far the clutch pedal is pressed, or how far an automated clutch is engaged.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine may not crank, or cruise control may not work
Jerky clutch engagement on automated manual transmissions

causes.name: Open or broken wire in the clutch position sensor circuit
Wire shorted to another power circuit

checks: Check the connector for pushed-out or loose pins
Check the clutch position sensor circuit for an open wire or a short to voltage
Test the clutch position sensor against the factory specification
fix: Repair the open or shorted wire or bad connector; if the wiring is good, replace the clutch position sensor.

title: Clutch Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent
plain: The signal from the clutch position sensor keeps dropping out or jumping around, which usually points to a loose connection or a damaged wire.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine may not crank, or cruise control may not work
Jerky clutch engagement on automated manual transmissions
Problem may come and go, often over bumps

causes.name: Chafed wiring that opens or shorts as it moves

checks: Wiggle-test the wiring and connector while watching live data
Look for rubbed-through wiring near brackets and moving parts
fix: Repair the loose connection or damaged wire; replace the clutch position sensor only if it fails testing.

title: Clutch Position Not Learned
plain: The computer has not yet learned the clutch engagement point, which it needs to control starting, cruise or an automated clutch correctly.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine may not crank, or clutch engagement may feel off
Cruise control may not work

causes.name: Clutch position relearn not done after a clutch, sensor or module replacement
Battery was disconnected or went dead

checks: Run the clutch position learn procedure with a scan tool
Check the clutch position sensor reading and adjustment
fix: Perform the clutch position relearn with a capable scan tool; replace the sensor only if it will not learn.

title: Clutch Position Control Error
plain: The computer is commanding the automated clutch to a position, but the clutch is not getting there as expected.
symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Jerky take-off or clutch slipping
Car may not move or may refuse a gear

causes.name: Worn clutch or clutch needing a relearn
Low hydraulic fluid or hydraulic leak

checks: Check for other clutch or actuator codes
Run the clutch adaptation relearn with a scan tool
Check hydraulic fluid level if the system uses one
fix: Relearn the clutch first; if the fault returns, repair the actuator or replace the worn clutch.

title: Excessive Clutch Slippage
plain: The computer sees the engine speed running higher than the transmission input speed while the clutch should be fully engaged, which means the clutch is slipping.
symptoms: Engine revs rise without the car speeding up
Burning smell after hard driving
Check engine light on

causes.name: Clutch hydraulic or actuator problem holding the clutch partly open

checks: Check clutch fluid level and look for leaks
Do a road test in a high gear at low speed to confirm slipping
Check for a rear main seal oil leak
fix: Usually a clutch replacement, fixing any oil leak at the same time.
drive: Drive as little as possible. A slipping clutch wears out quickly and can get worse suddenly. If the engine revs rise but the car doesn't speed up, or you smell burning, avoid highways and hills and consider a tow. Short, gentle trips to a shop soon at most.

title: Reverse Input Circuit
plain: There is an electrical problem in the circuit that tells the computer reverse gear has been selected.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Backup lights or backup camera may not work

causes.name: Failed reverse switch or range sensor

checks: Check whether the backup lights come on in reverse
Inspect the reverse switch or range sensor connector
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the reverse switch or range sensor.

title: Reverse Output Circuit
plain: There is an electrical problem in the circuit the computer uses to send out the reverse signal to other systems, such as the backup lights.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Backup lights or backup camera may not work

causes.name: Damaged or shorted wiring in the reverse output circuit
Problem in a module or lamp circuit that receives the signal

checks: Check whether backup lights and camera work in reverse
Check the reverse output wire for an open or short
fix: Repair the wiring fault in the reverse output circuit.

title: Transmission Range Display Circuit
plain: The circuit that drives the gear position display (P R N D) on the dash has an electrical problem.
symptoms: Gear indicator may be blank or wrong
Check engine light on

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector to the display

checks: Check whether the gear display works at all
Check the display circuit wiring for opens or shorts
fix: Repair the display wiring or the instrument cluster.

title: Upshift Switch Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the up and down shift switch, which sends your manual upshift and downshift requests (from the shifter or paddles) to the transmission computer. This code is for the upshift switch.
symptoms: Manual or paddle shifting may not work
Check engine light on
Normal automatic shifting in Drive usually still works

causes.name: Broken or damaged wiring to the shift switch
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the shift switch for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the shift switch against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the shift switch.

title: Downshift Switch Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the up and down shift switch, which sends your manual upshift and downshift requests (from the shifter or paddles) to the transmission computer. This code is for the downshift switch.
symptoms: Manual or paddle shifting may not work
Check engine light on
Normal automatic shifting in Drive usually still works

causes.name: Broken or damaged wiring to the shift switch
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the shift switch for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the shift switch against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the shift switch.

title: Starter Disable Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the starter disable circuit, which lets the computer block the starter unless it is safe to crank, such as in Park or with the clutch pressed.
symptoms: Engine may not crank, or only cranks some of the time
Check engine light on

causes.name: Failed starter relay or starter disable relay
Broken or damaged wiring to the starter disable circuit
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the starter disable circuit for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the starter disable circuit against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the starter disable circuit.

title: Driveline Disconnect Switch Input Circuit
plain: There is an electrical problem in the switch circuit that tells the computer whether part of the driveline has been disconnected, as on some 4WD and hybrid systems.
symptoms: Check engine light on
4WD or AWD may not engage or disengage properly
checks: Inspect the switch connector for corrosion or damage
Watch the switch status on a scan tool while engaging and disengaging
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the disconnect switch.

title: Up and Down Shift Switch to Transmission Range Correlation
plain: The manual up/down shift switch signal does not agree with the gear range the transmission says it is in.
symptoms: Manual or paddle shifting may not work
Check engine light on

causes.name: Transmission range sensor out of adjustment or failing

checks: Compare the shift switch and range sensor readings on a scan tool
Check range sensor and shift cable adjustment
fix: Adjust or replace the range sensor or the up/down shift switch, whichever reads wrong.

title: Starter Disable Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the starter disable circuit that is lower than it should be. The starter disable circuit lets the computer block the starter unless it is safe to crank, such as in Park or with the clutch pressed.
symptoms: Engine may not crank, or only cranks some of the time
Check engine light on

causes.name: Wire shorted to ground in the starter disable circuit circuit
Failed starter relay or starter disable relay (internal short)

checks: Inspect the starter disable circuit wiring for chafed spots touching metal
Check the circuit for a short to ground with a meter
Unplug the starter disable circuit and see whether the reading changes
fix: Fix any shorted or damaged wiring; if the wiring is good, replace the starter disable circuit.

title: Starter Disable Circuit High
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the starter disable circuit that is higher than it should be. The starter disable circuit lets the computer block the starter unless it is safe to crank, such as in Park or with the clutch pressed.
symptoms: Engine may not crank, or only cranks some of the time
Check engine light on

causes.name: Open or broken wire in the starter disable circuit circuit
Failed starter relay or starter disable relay
Wire shorted to another power circuit

checks: Check the connector for pushed-out or loose pins
Check the starter disable circuit circuit for an open wire or a short to voltage
Test the starter disable circuit against the factory specification
fix: Repair the open or shorted wire or bad connector; if the wiring is good, replace the starter disable circuit.

title: Park Input Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit that tells it the transmission is in Park.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine may not crank, or may only crank in Neutral
Gear indicator or idle quality may be slightly off

causes.name: Switch or shift cable out of adjustment
Broken or damaged wiring to the park/neutral switch
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the park/neutral switch for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the park/neutral switch against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the park/neutral switch.

title: Neutral Input Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit that tells it the transmission is in Neutral.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine may not crank, or may only crank in Neutral
Gear indicator or idle quality may be slightly off

causes.name: Switch or shift cable out of adjustment
Broken or damaged wiring to the park/neutral switch
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the park/neutral switch for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the park/neutral switch against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the park/neutral switch.

title: Gear Lever X-Y Position Sensor Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the gear lever position sensor, which tells the transmission computer where the shift lever is on shift-by-wire or automated manual systems. This code is for the combined X-Y position sensor circuit.
symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Gear selected may not match the lever, or gears may be refused
Transmission may go into a default gear

causes.name: Broken or damaged wiring to the gear lever sensor
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the gear lever sensor for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the gear lever sensor against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the gear lever sensor.

title: Gear Lever X Position Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the gear lever position sensor, which tells the transmission computer where the shift lever is on shift-by-wire or automated manual systems. This code is for the X position signal.
symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Gear selected may not match the lever, or gears may be refused
Transmission may go into a default gear

causes.name: Broken or damaged wiring to the gear lever sensor
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the gear lever sensor for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the gear lever sensor against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the gear lever sensor.

symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Gear selected may not match the lever, or gears may be refused
Transmission may go into a default gear

causes.name: Broken or damaged wiring to the gear lever sensor
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the gear lever sensor for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the gear lever sensor against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the gear lever sensor.

title: Gear Lever X Position Circuit Intermittent
plain: The signal from the gear lever position sensor keeps dropping out or jumping around, which usually points to a loose connection or a damaged wire. This code is for the X position signal.
symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Gear selected may not match the lever, or gears may be refused
Transmission may go into a default gear
Problem may come and go, often over bumps

causes.name: Chafed wiring that opens or shorts as it moves

checks: Wiggle-test the wiring and connector while watching live data
Look for rubbed-through wiring near brackets and moving parts
fix: Repair the loose connection or damaged wire; replace the gear lever sensor only if it fails testing.

title: Gear Lever Push-Pull Switch (Shift Anticipate)
plain: The switch that senses you are about to push or pull the gear lever has a fault, so the transmission computer cannot prepare for the shift.
symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light on
Slower or rougher shifts

causes.name: Failed push-pull switch in the shifter

checks: Watch the switch status on a scan tool while moving the lever
Inspect the shifter wiring and connector
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the shifter switch or shifter assembly.

title: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the up and down shift switch, which sends your manual upshift and downshift requests (from the shifter or paddles) to the transmission computer. This code is for the shared up and down shift switch circuit.
symptoms: Manual or paddle shifting may not work
Check engine light on
Normal automatic shifting in Drive usually still works

causes.name: Broken or damaged wiring to the shift switch
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the shift switch for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the shift switch against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the shift switch.

title: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the up and down shift switch circuit that is lower than it should be. The shift switch sends your manual upshift and downshift requests (from the shifter or paddles) to the transmission computer.
symptoms: Manual or paddle shifting may not work
Check engine light on
Normal automatic shifting in Drive usually still works

causes.name: Wire shorted to ground in the shift switch circuit

checks: Inspect the shift switch wiring for chafed spots touching metal
Check the circuit for a short to ground with a meter
Unplug the shift switch and see whether the reading changes
fix: Fix any shorted or damaged wiring; if the wiring is good, replace the shift switch.

Check the shift switch circuit for an open wire or a short to voltage

fix: Repair the open or shorted wire or bad connector; if the wiring is good, replace the shift switch.

title: 5-6 Shift
plain: The transmission computer found a problem with the shift between 5th and 6th gear: it took too long, did not happen, or did not feel right.
symptoms: Check engine light on
No 6th gear or a flare during the 5-6 shift
Higher engine speed on the highway

causes.name: Shift solenoid or valve body problem
Worn clutch pack inside the transmission
Control module software needs an update

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Check for software updates or service bulletins (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
Watch the 5-6 shift on a scan tool during a road test
fix: Correct the fluid and check for updates first; solenoid or internal repair may be needed.

title: Clutch Pedal Switch A Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the clutch pedal switch A, which tells the computer when the clutch pedal is pressed, which matters for starting and cruise control.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine may not crank with the clutch pressed
Cruise control may not work or may not cancel

causes.name: Switch out of adjustment at the pedal
Broken or damaged wiring to the clutch pedal switch
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the clutch pedal switch for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the clutch pedal switch against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the clutch pedal switch.

title: Clutch Pedal Switch A Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the clutch pedal switch A circuit that is lower than it should be. The clutch pedal switch tells the computer when the clutch pedal is pressed, which matters for starting and cruise control.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine may not crank with the clutch pressed
Cruise control may not work or may not cancel

Switch out of adjustment at the pedal

checks: Inspect the clutch pedal switch wiring for chafed spots touching metal
Check the circuit for a short to ground with a meter
Unplug the clutch pedal switch and see whether the reading changes
fix: Fix any shorted or damaged wiring; if the wiring is good, replace the clutch pedal switch.
